books.section: Topic 4.10 The Second Great Awakening, Transcendentalism

primary_sources: Henry David Thoreau, "Resistance to Civil Government" (1849)

stimulus.text: Henry David Thoreau, Walden; or, Life in the Woods (1854): "I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived." Thoreau built a cabin at Walden Pond near Concord, Massachusetts, and lived there for two years, from 1845 to 1847.
stimulus.source_note: Verbatim quotation from Henry David Thoreau, Walden; or, Life in the Woods (1854). Public domain; wording checked against the published text. The cabin dates are from the book's account.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: Thoreau's later essay on civil disobedience (1849) applied the same thinking to politics by arguing which of the following?

options.text: Citizens should always obey the law, whatever it commands
options.misconception: Most writers on government stress obedience, so it is easy to assume Thoreau did too.

options.text: Conscience outranking law, and refusal to support unjust government
Only judges may decide whether a law is just
options.misconception: Courts decide laws, so it is easy to hand the whole question to judges.

options.text: Voting is the only proper way to protest
options.misconception: Voting is the usual protest, so it is easy to think Thoreau allowed no other.

rationales.A: Thoreau argued the opposite: obedience to an unjust law is itself a failure of conscience.
rationales.B: The essay grew from Thoreau's own night in jail for refusing a poll tax during the Mexican War.
rationales.C: Thoreau put the decision in each person's conscience, not in a courtroom.
rationales.D: Thoreau refused to pay the tax itself; his protest was a deed, not only a ballot.
rationales.general:
1. Carry the Walden idea into politics. If the self must live deliberately, it must also judge the laws it lives under.
2. Recall the deed behind the essay. Thoreau spent a night in jail rather than pay a tax to a government at war.
Background: the essay was written after his 1846 arrest for refusing the poll tax during the Mexican War.
Remember: a philosophy of the self becomes a politics the moment it meets a law.
